answer_text:
Here is a comprehensive guide to the temperatures at which food can be accepted upon delivery:

---

## 🌡️ Food Receiving Temperature Guidelines

### 🥶 Cold TCS (Temperature Control for Safety) Foods
Receive **cold TCS food** at **41°F (5°C) or lower**, unless otherwise specified.

### 🔥 Hot Foods
Receive **hot TCS food** at **135°F (57°C) or higher.**

### 🧊 Frozen Foods
**Frozen food** should be **frozen solid** when received.

---

### 🦪 Special Categories

| Food Item | Acceptable Receiving Temperature |
|---|---|
| **Live Shellfish** (oysters, mussels, clams, scallops) | Air temperature of **45°F (7°C)** and internal temp no greater than **50°F (10°C)** |
| **Shucked Shellfish** | **45°F (7°C) or lower** |
| **Milk** | **45°F (7°C) or lower** |
| **Shell Eggs** | Air temperature of **45°F (7°C) or lower** |

---

### ⚠️ The Temperature Danger Zone
Harmful microorganisms grow well in foods held between **41°F and 135°F** — this range is known as the **Temperature Danger Zone (TDZ)**.

When food sits in the danger zone between 41°F and 135°F, bacteria can **double every 20 minutes**.

---

### ❌ When to Reject Food
Reject any **cold items above 41°F** or **frozen items showing signs of thawing**. Verify hot deliveries arrive at **135°F or above** if applicable.

You should also reject food with packaging issues:
- Reject items with **tears, holes, or punctures** in packaging, as well as cans with **bulging or swollen ends, rust, or dents**.
- **Never accept home-canned foods** because of the risk of botulism.

---

### 🌡️ Thermometer Tips
A **probe thermometer** is a simple tool that can help ensure the quality and safety of the food your restaurant receives by verifying its temperature. Measure the temperature at **multiple points**, especially in the **middle and thicker sections**, to ensure it has reached the required safe temperature.
